Hi Amit / Elena 

Thanks again for the call today  great to get aligned on your integration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps around API auth and key management so we can scope the technical deep-dive: 

1) Key auth patterns discussed
   - API keys (simple, long-lived)
   - Service accounts + short-lived tokens (recommended for production)
   - OAuth2/JWT client_credentials for server-to-server flows

2) FintechCo asks we noted
   - Prefer service-account style auth with KMS-backed signing and automated rotation
   - Per-environment isolation (staging/prod) + scoped keys for embeddings vs. model inference
   - Audit logs and ability to revoke keys immediately

3) Redwood capabilities (high-level)
   - Per-service-account objects in Console + RBAC (grant by model / route)
   - Support for API keys and OAuth2/JWT flows; optional integration with customer KMS/HSM
   - Key rotation APIs and short-lived token issuance (token TTL configurable)
   - Token claims can be restricted to routes/models for routing/segmentation (helpful for embeddings/rerankers)

Next steps / asks for you:
   - Please confirm whether you want Redwood to manage signing keys (we rotate and store) or if you will provide JWKS / KMS integration for signing.
   - Security team: if you have a short checklist or mandatory controls (e.g., key TTL max, rotation cadence) please send it over so we can map to our config.
   - Technical walkthrough: Rishi (SE) can run a 30-min session to show SDK flows, rotation, and per-route scoping.

Proposed timeline: if you confirm managed keys vs customer-managed KMS this week, we can schedule the SE walkthrough for next week and deliver a Mutual Action Plan.

Thanks Marissa  really helpful summary. A few answers / clarifications from our side: 

- We prefer a service-account model with short-lived tokens issued by our infra (we run HashiCorp Vault + AWS KMS). Ideally Redwood would accept signed JWTs from our signing service, or we can configure a JWKS endpoint.
- We want per-environment separation (staging/prod) and separate credentials for embeddings ingestion vs real-time inference/reranking (so we can track usage and billing).
- Rotation: security prefers automatic rotation of signing keys with monthly rotation and ability to revoke immediately. For tokens we prefer TTL <= 24h if feasible.

Hi Amit / Elena 

Quick technical notes ahead of the walkthrough. TL;DR: service accounts + short-lived JWTs (client_credentials) is the safest pattern; we support either Redwood-managed signing keys or customer-managed JWKS/KMS.

Recommended integration pattern (option A and B):

Option A  Customer-managed signing (preferred for compliance):
 1) FintechCo runs signing keys in Vault/KMS and exposes a JWKS endpoint (or uses a short-lived signing service).
 2) Create a service account in Redwood Console and configure the service account to accept tokens signed by your JWKS (we validate signatures + claims).
 3) Tokens should include claims for allowed_routes / scopes so we can do routing/quotas per workload (e.g., embeddings vs. rerank).
 4) You rotate the signing key; Redwood supports key id (kid) validation and immediate revocation if you remove a kid from your JWKS.

Option B  Redwood-managed keys (faster setup):
 1) We create a service account and Redwood generates a signing key which we can store in our HSM/KMS.
 2) We provide a short-lived access token via a client_credentials flow; you can call a token endpoint to exchange a service account credential for a short-lived token.
 3) We support automated rotation and provide audit logs for key operations.

Practical recommendations:
- Token TTL: 24h or less for high-security workloads; for internal jobs you can use longer TTLs but still rotate keys monthly.
- Per-workload service accounts: create separate service accounts for embeddings ingestion, retrievers/rerankers, and realtime chat inference so you can isolate permissions & billing.
- Scoping: include allowed_routes and model_id in token claims; Redwood uses these to do routing and apply per-route SLOs.
- Revocation: we support immediate revocation via Console/API.

SDK notes (pseudo):
  // server side: exchange client credential for short-lived token
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: new ServiceAccountAuth({ tokenEndpoint: 'https://auth.fintechco.com/token' }) });
  const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood-embedding-1' });

Docs / walkthrough links:
  - https://redwood.ai/docs/auth#service-accounts
  - https://redwood.ai/docs/rotation
